To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

for a large class of self-similarity systems, the dimension of sections of a self-similar set is at least the dimension of the set minus 1, and that the set of exceptions is a set of Hausdorf dimension 0.

for a class of self similar sets, the Hausdorfr dimensions of sections of the sets are almost everywhere equal to the Hausdorrr dimensions of the sets, and for a class of percolation sets, the box dimensions of sections are almost everywhere equal the box dimensions of the sets.
for a wide class of self-similarity sets, the Hausdorfr and box dimensions of the sections of the sets are close to the dimension of the set itself.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question.
a new method to prove dimension conservation theorems for fractal sets.
the study of the dimensions of sections, projections, and intersections of sets with fractal structure, and their connections to other fractal dimensions of the sets.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
for a large class of sets, the dimensions of sections are almost as large as possible.
for a large class of sets, the dimension of a section of a set of positive Hausdorff or box dimension is positive, and for a smaller class, the dimension of the section of the set is at least 1.
the dimensions of sections are not too far from the dimension of the set, and that the directions for which this is not true form a set of dimension 0.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a large class of sets, we obtain dimension conservation for sections of Hausdorrf dimension greater than 1.
for a large class of self-similarity and percolation sets we establish dimension conservation for sections.
for a large class of sets, the dimension of the sections is not much smaller than the dimension of the original set, and the exceptions are of dimension 0.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fractal percolations can be used to establish dimension conservation for sections of deterministic sets.
the dimension of sections of a fractal is often close to the dimension of the fractal, even when the sections are small and far apart.
the dimension of sections of a self-similar set is not affected by the dimension of the set, but only the dimension of the rotational components of its generating similarities.
